themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees/Branches Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Tree and branch complaints surged to 19 this week versus a 3.8-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 407% spike (z-score: 9.3)—suggesting either storm damage, seasonal growth, or deferred maintenance becoming suddenly visible in Astoria/Long Island City.
evidence: 19 overgrown tree/branch complaints this week vs. 3.8 weekly average (407% increase, z-score: 9.3)
Highest statistical anomaly in dataset after mobile food vendor spike
Timing suggests acute trigger: recent weather event or seasonal growth acceleration
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Walk streets in Astoria and Long Island City this week to document which blocks have hazardous branches; interview residents about safety concerns
Process investigation: How quickly does Parks & Recreation respond to overgrown tree complaints? Are there backlog issues at DOT?

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about mobile food vendors jumped 522% this week (7 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average, z-score: 9.8)—the single largest statistical anomaly—suggesting either sudden proliferation, enforcement action, or concentrated resident frustration in a specific area.
evidence: 7 mobile food vendor complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (522% spike, z-score: 9.8)
Highest z-score in entire dataset—statistically extreme outlier
No supporting context from Reddit, news mentions, or community board suggests this is highly localized
reporting_angles: Cartography: Map the 7 complaints to see if they cluster on one block (near transit hub, park, school?) or are dispersed
Enforcement angle: Did the city launch a licensing/enforcement sweep this week? Interview vendors and Department of Health about recent activity

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints nearly doubled this week (100 complaints vs. 43.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 129% increase, z-score: 4.64)—coinciding with warm weather, outdoor dining season, and multiple rezoning proposals that may be triggering development and activity.
evidence: 100 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 43.8 weekly average (129% increase, z-score: 4.64)
Outdoor dining complaints also elevated 2 weeks ago (9 vs. 1.1 avg, 700% spike, z-score: 6.21)
Timing aligns with seasonal warm weather and active outdoor dining season in Astoria/LIC waterfront areas
reporting_angles: Sidewalk reporting: Identify top complaint blocks and document commercial activity: bars, restaurants, construction, delivery noise
Zoning angle: Do ULURP projects in review (33-01 11th Street, 43-02 Ditmars rezoning) correlate with complaint clusters? Are new venues opening in anticipation of rezoning?

themes_detail.label: General 311 Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Unspecified 'general' 311 complaints doubled this week (52 complaints vs. 23.6 weekly baseline—a 120% increase, z-score: 6.05)—a catch-all signal that may indicate either system miscoding or genuine resident frustration about issues not fitting standard categories.
evidence: 52 general complaints this week vs. 23.6 weekly baseline (120% spike, z-score: 6.05)
No thematic clustering provided in data—suggests either system routing problem or diverse, unmapped resident issues
Timing aligns with tree/mobile vendor/commercial noise spikes, suggesting possible underlying neighborhood stress
reporting_angles: Data transparency: Request from DOF a sample of 10 'general' complaints filed this week to understand what residents are actually reporting
Sentiment check: Scan Astoria/LIC Facebook groups and NextDoor for complaints from past 7 days to triangulate themes

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, Juno) jumped 309% two weeks ago (23 complaints vs. 5.6 weekly average, z-score: 6.15)—sustained elevation suggesting congestion, illegal parking, or aggressive driving behavior tied to rideshare density in Astoria/Long Island City.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.6 weekly baseline (309% spike, z-score: 6.15)
Aligns with broader pattern: illegal parking remains #1 complaint (6,268 over 90 days), blocked driveways #3 (1,771)
No recent Streetsblog or news coverage of FHV activity in district suggests undercovered problem
reporting_angles: Hot spot mapping: Use 311 geolocation data to identify which blocks (near subway stations, waterfront, offices?) drive FHV complaints
Driver angle: Interview rideshare drivers about parking/idling practices; interview residents about congestion impact on school zones or residential blocks
